mainTopic: Why women forbidden by a לאו do חליצה and not יבום: a Torah rule or a rabbinic גזירה?
overview: The גמרא explains that חייבי לאוין still need חליצה while חייבי כריתות do not, because קידושין take effect with the first group but not with the second. רבא then challenges the view that, by Torah law, חייבי לאוין need חליצה but are never subject to יבום. His first challenge, about relations exempting the צרה, he answers himself. His second, a ברייתא saying that a פצוע דכא who does יבום still acquires the woman, forces a new approach. רבא tries saying an אלמנה מן האירוסין is forbidden to a כהן גדול by an עשה and a לאו, but that would make every לאו in the Torah an עשה too. So he explains the ban as a rabbinic גזירה. The גמרא tests that גזירה against several cases where no decree is made, and it falls apart because a ממזרת and a נתינה are rare. רבא then says the first ביאה was banned because of the second ביאה, and a ברייתא supports this. He briefly retracts in favor of ריש לקיש's rule that an עשה does not override a לאו when both can be kept, but a ברייתא refutes that, so the rabbinic decree stands. Finally, רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר argue whether a כהן גדול's ביאה with his widowed יבמה frees her צרה.

steps.title: Why women forbidden by a לאו need חליצה but women forbidden under כרת do not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the difference: קידושין take effect with חייבי לאוין, so the bond with the יבם is real and needs חליצה. קידושין do not take effect with חייבי כריתות, so יבום and חליצה do not apply at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense: with women forbidden by a לאו, קידושין take effect. With women forbidden under כרת, קידושין do not take effect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a logical reason why women forbidden by a לאו are treated differently from women forbidden under כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a man does קידושין with a woman forbidden to him by a לאו, the קידושין still work, even though he sinned. So a real legal bond can exist, and that is why חליצה is needed. With חייבי כריתות, קידושין never take hold, so there is nothing for יבום or חליצה to act on.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason; it makes sense logically
Relationships forbidden by a plain negative commandment (a לאו)
Relationships forbidden under the punishment of כרת
Betrothal takes effect with them

steps.whyThisMatters: This principle (קידושין work with חייבי לאוין but not with חייבי כריתות) is the reason the two groups are handled so differently throughout the laws of יבום.

phrases.english: It stands to reason: those forbidden by a negative commandment —
betrothal takes effect with them.
Those forbidden under karet —
betrothal does not take effect with them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from before this section: why do חייבי לאוין need חליצה when חייבי כריתות do not?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference depends on whether קידושין can take effect: they can with חייבי לאוין, but they cannot with חייבי כריתות.

steps.title: רבא challenges from a ברייתא: relations exempt the צרה
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a ברייתא: if the יבם has relations with, or does חליצה with, a woman under an איסור מצוה or איסור קדושה, her צרה is exempt. If חייבי לאוין are not subject to יבום by Torah law, how could relations exempt the צרה?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected: with an איסור מצוה or an איסור קדושה, if he had relations with her or did חליצה with her, her צרה is exempt. But if you think חייבי לאוין need חליצה by Torah law and are not subject to יבום, then when he has relations with her, why is her צרה exempt?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the view that, by Torah law, women forbidden by a לאו need only חליצה and never יבום. He brings a ברייתא that seems to say relations with such a woman count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A צרה is only exempted by a valid act of יבום or חליצה. If the Torah gives no יבום at all to an איסור קדושה (a woman forbidden by a לאו), then relations with her should be legally meaningless. Yet the ברייתא says they exempt the צרה.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection (usually from a תנאי source)
A prohibition from the Rabbis (the second-degree relatives)
A prohibition of holiness, meaning a woman forbidden by a Torah לאו
Her rival wife, the other widow of the same dead brother
Does not fall upon him; is not obligated

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection:
A prohibition of מצוה and a prohibition of sanctity,
phrases.notes: These are the two groups from the משנה: rabbinic second-degree relatives, and women forbidden by a Torah לאו.

phrases.english: if he had relations with her or performed chalitza with her —
her rival wife is exempt.
And if it should enter your mind
that those forbidden by a negative commandment require chalitza by Torah law,
but are not subject to levirate marriage,
then when he had relations with her —
why is her rival wife exempt?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the position being defended, that חייבי לאוין need חליצה but not יבום by Torah law.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that by Torah law חייבי לאוין are subject to חליצה but not to יבום.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says relations with an איסור קדושה exempt the צרה. That could only be true if יבום with her is valid by Torah law.

steps.title: רבא answers himself: the ברייתא speaks of two separate cases
steps.stepSummary: רבא resolves his own question. The ברייתא is split: 'had relations' refers only to the איסור מצוה, and 'did חליצה' refers to the איסור קדושה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He raised the objection and he resolved it: the ברייתא teaches the cases separately. 'Had relations with her' refers to the איסור מצוה. 'Did חליצה with her' refers to the איסור קדושה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers his own challenge by saying the two verbs in the ברייתא do not apply to both groups of women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The איסור מצוה is only rabbinic, so by Torah law יבום with her is valid, and relations exempt the צרה. The איסור קדושה is a Torah לאו, so only חליצה works for her. Read this way, the ברייתא fits the view that חייבי לאוין get חליצה but not יבום.

keyTerms.term: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ
keyTerms.meaning: He raised the objection, and he himself resolved it
It is taught in separate parts; each clause refers to a different case

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the ברייתא as saying both actions work for both women. Each action is matched to only one of the two groups.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's first challenge is resolved: relations work only for the rabbinic איסור מצוה, while the Torah-level איסור קדושה needs חליצה.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ:
phrases.english: He raised the objection and he resolved it:
It is teaching the cases separately.
'Had relations with her' — refers to the prohibition of מצוה.
'Performed chalitza with her' — refers to the prohibition of sanctity.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge from step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the source: the ברייתא is split into separate cases (לצדדין).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say relations work even for an איסור קדושה, a woman forbidden by a Torah לאו.
steps.terutzMaskana: Relations exempt the צרה only for the rabbinic איסור מצוה. For the איסור קדושה, only חליצה does.

steps.title: רבא raises a new challenge about men who cannot have children
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a ברייתא about a פצוע דכא, a כרות שפכה, a סריס אדם and an elderly man: they either do חליצה or יבום. Whatever the brothers did (מאמר, גט, חליצה) is valid, and if they had relations, they acquired the women.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected: a פצוע דכא, a כרות שפכה, a man made a סריס by people, and an elderly man either do חליצה or do יבום. How so? If they died, and they had brothers and wives, and the brothers went ahead and did מאמר with their wives, or gave a גט, or did חליצה, what they did is done. And if they had relations, they acquired them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is setting up a second challenge to the same view. He quotes the source here, and the next part of the גמרא will explain exactly what the problem is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This first half is the simple case: the infertile men died, and their healthy brothers did יבום with the widows, so there is no prohibition at all. The challenge comes from the reverse case in the next part of the ברייתא, where the infertile men themselves, who are forbidden by a לאו, do יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: A man with crushed or wounded testicles
A man whose organ has been cut off
A man made unable to father children by human action, not from birth
Rabbinic betrothal of a יבמה before יבום
They acquired her as a wife

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection:
A man with crushed testicles, and one whose organ is severed,
a eunuch made by man, and an elderly man —
either perform chalitza or perform levirate marriage.
How so?
If they died, and they had brothers and they had wives,
and the brothers went ahead and made a levirate betrothal with their wives,
or gave a bill of divorce, or performed chalitza —
what they did is done.
And if they had relations — they acquired.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge is resolved, רבא brings a second source against the same view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that by Torah law חייבי לאוין are subject to חליצה but not to יבום.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This half only sets up the source. The attack comes from the second half, in step 5: there the פצוע דכא, who is forbidden by a לאו, does יבום, and the ברייתא still says 'קנו'.

steps.title: The rest of the ברייתא: relations by these men acquire the woman
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: when the brothers die, these men's מאמר, גט and חליצה all count, and relations acquire the יבמה, even though they may not stay married. The גמרא asks: if חייבי לאוין have no יבום by Torah law, how can relations acquire her?
steps.simpleTranslation: If the brothers died, and these men gave a מאמר to the widows, or a גט, or did חליצה, what they did counts. If they had relations, they acquired the women, but they may not stay married to them, because the פסוק says 'a פצוע דכא shall not enter.' Now, if חייבי לאוין only need חליצה by Torah law and are not open to יבום, why would relations acquire them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the ברייתא it started quoting and turns it into a challenge. It asks against the view that חייבי לאוין need חליצה but cannot have יבום by Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These men are forbidden to marry a Jewish woman because of a לאו, so their widowed sisters-in-law are חייבי לאוין to them. Yet the ברייתא says relations with her 'acquire' her, which is the language of real יבום. That only makes sense if יבום does apply to חייבי לאוין by Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: A man whose reproductive organs are crushed; the Torah forbids him to marry into the community
They acquired, meaning the יבום took effect and she became his wife
Forbidden to keep them as wives
Falls upon, applies to

steps.confusionAlert: 'קנו' and 'אסור לקיימן' do not contradict each other. The יבום really works, but he must still divorce her because of the לאו.

phrases.english: If the brothers died, and they proceeded
phrases.notes: 'They' are the men just listed: the פצוע דכא, כרות שפכה and so on. Now they are the surviving brothers.

phrases.english: and made a מאמר with their wives
and gave a גט, or did חליצה
what they did is done.
And if they had relations, they acquired them,
but it is forbidden to keep them,
because it says: 'A פצוע דכא shall not enter.'
Now, if you think
that by Torah law חייבי לאוין are subject to חליצה
but not subject to יבום,
then if they had relations, why did they acquire her?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 4 and turns it into the actual challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that חייבי לאוין need חליצה but have no יבום by Torah law
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says relations by men forbidden through a לאו acquire the יבמה, so יבום must apply to חייבי לאוין.

steps.title: רבא: אלמנה מן האירוסין is both an עשה and a לא תעשה
steps.stepSummary: רבא drops the earlier approach. He explains that a כהן גדול with an אלמנה מן האירוסין is forbidden by an עשה as well as a לאו, because of the פסוק 'קדושים יהיו לאלהיהם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: an אלמנה מן האירוסין is also a case of an עשה together with a לא תעשה, as it is written: 'They shall be holy to their God.'
steps.whatsHappening: Since the earlier approach failed, רבא gives a new reason why a כהן גדול cannot do יבום with an אלמנה מן האירוסין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the עשה of יבום overrides a plain לאו. But an עשה cannot override a prohibition that has both a לאו and an עשה. רבא reads 'קדושים יהיו' as adding an עשה to the כהנים' marriage prohibitions, so יבום cannot push this one aside.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman widowed after קידושין but before נשואין
A prohibition made of both a positive and a negative commandment
Rather, which drops the previous approach

phrases.english: Rather, רבא said:
A widow from betrothal, too,
phrases.notes: He means she is forbidden to a כהן גדול, which is the case the sugya is trying to explain.

phrases.english: is an עשה and a לא תעשה,
as it is written: 'They shall be holy to their God.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 5 disproves the earlier view, רבא offers a new explanation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reasoning that replaces the rejected approach
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The block on יבום comes from חייבי לאוין having no יבום at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The block comes from the prohibition being both an עשה and a לאו, which the עשה of יבום cannot override.

steps.title: What about a ממזרת and a נתינה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the פסוק 'קדושים יהיו' covers only כהנים. What adds an עשה to the bans on a ממזרת and a נתינה?
steps.simpleTranslation: A ממזרת and a נתינה: what is there to say about them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's new idea. His פסוק covers only the כהנים, so it does not explain other forbidden women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ממזרת and a נתינה are also forbidden by a לאו and are not open to יבום. The פסוק about כהנים does not reach them, so where would their עשה come from?

keyTerms.meaning: A woman born from a forbidden union, who is not allowed to marry into the community
A woman descended from the גבעונים, who is not allowed to marry into the community
What is there to say? This asks for an explanation.

phrases.english: A ממזרת and a נתינה,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רבא's answer from step 6 on cases outside the כהנים.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's use of 'קדושים יהיו' to add an עשה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That פסוק is limited to כהנים, so it cannot explain why a ממזרת or נתינה has no יבום.

steps.title: The answer: 'והתקדשתם'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the general פסוק 'והתקדשתם' adds an עשה to these prohibitions as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written: 'You shall make yourselves holy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question about ממזרת and נתינה with a broader פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'והתקדשתם' is addressed to all of ישראל, not only כהנים. So it seems to give these bans an עשה too, and יבום cannot override them.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You shall make yourselves holy,' a general command of holiness

phrases.english: It is written: 'You shall make yourselves holy.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only כהנים have an added עשה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'והתקדשתם' adds an עשה to these other prohibitions too.

steps.title: Then the whole Torah would be עשה and לא תעשה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects that answer: 'והתקדשתם' applies to everything, so every לאו in the Torah would become an עשה plus a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the entire Torah would also be an עשה and a לא תעשה, since it is written: 'You shall make yourselves holy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 8 by showing it proves too much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'והתקדשתם' turns a לאו into an עשה plus a לאו, then every לאו would have that status. Then the rule that an עשה overrides a לא תעשה could never apply anywhere, which cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, which pushes an idea to its extreme result
The entire Torah

phrases.english: If so,
the entire Torah, too,
is an עשה and a לא תעשה,
since it is written: 'You shall make yourselves holy'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the answer in step 8, and the approach of step 6 built on it, proves too much.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using 'והתקדשתם' to add an עשה to a לאו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reductio ad absurdum: every לאו in the Torah would become an עשה and a לאו, so עשה דוחה לא תעשה would never work.

steps.title: רבא: a rabbinic גזירה because of an אלמנה מן הנשואין
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a new answer. By Torah law יבום would apply, but the רבנן forbade an אלמנה מן האירוסין to a כהן גדול so people would not do the same with an אלמנה מן הנשואין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: it is a גזירה. An אלמנה מן האירוסין is forbidden because of an אלמנה מן הנשואין.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא drops the עשה-and-לאו idea and explains the ban as a rabbinic decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אלמנה מן הנשואין is no longer a בתולה, so for a כהן גדול she falls under both a לאו and the עשה of 'בתולה מעמיו יקח', and the עשה of יבום cannot override that. An אלמנה מן האירוסין is still a בתולה, so by Torah law יבום would override her לאו alone. The רבנן banned it anyway so people would not mix up the two cases.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made to protect against a mistake
Because of, so as not to confuse with
A woman widowed after full marriage

steps.whatToRemember: New position: an אלמנה מן האירוסין with a כהן גדול would allow יבום by Torah law. The ban is a rabbinic גזירה, so people do not confuse her with an אלמנה מן הנשואין. The next steps test this idea, and in step 22 רבא replaces it with a different reason for the גזירה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This replaces two failed Torah-law explanations with a rabbinic one. It keeps both the rule that עשה דוחה לא תעשה and the ברייתא's ruling that חייבי לאוין are open to יבום.

phrases.english: Rather, רבא said:
It is a decree: a widow from betrothal is forbidden
because of a widow from marriage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 9 knocks out the עשה-and-לאו approach, רבא offers a rabbinic reason instead.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the ban from Torah law to rabbinic law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ban on יבום is from the Torah, as an עשה and a לאו.
steps.terutzMaskana: By Torah law יבום applies; the רבנן forbade it because of an אלמנה מן הנשואין.

steps.title: What about a ממזרת and a נתינה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבא's reason for the רבנן's ban works for a ממזרת or a נתינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ממזרת and a נתינה: what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's answer from Step 10. His reason works for a כהן גדול, but what reason is there for a ממזרת or a נתינה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a כהן גדול there is a similar case to worry about: an אלמנה מן הנשואין, who is always forbidden to him. For a ממזרת or a נתינה there is no 'other kind of widow' to mix up with, so רבא's reason seems to fall away. The גמרא wants to know what the reason for the ban would be here.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman born from a forbidden relationship. She is forbidden by a לאו to marry a regular ישראל.
A woman from the גבעונים, who are forbidden to marry into ישראל.
'What is there to say?' The גמרא is asking for an explanation that seems to be missing.

phrases.english: A mamzeret and a Gibeonite woman
phrases.notes: He means a brother's widow who is a ממזרת or a נתינה, so she is forbidden to a regular ישראל.

phrases.english: what is there to say?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer from Step 10. That answer worked for a כהן גדול but leaves the ממזרת and נתינה cases without a reason.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's explanation that the ban is a גזירה because of a similar forbidden case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For a ממזרת or a נתינה, there is no parallel 'always-forbidden' case for people to confuse with this one, so the reason does not fit.

steps.title: A ban in a מצוה case because of non-מצוה cases
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן forbade the ממזרת even when the מצוה of יבום applies, so people would not think she is allowed when there is no מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a גזירה: forbidding her where there is a מצוה, because of cases where there is no מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ban here comes from a different kind of worry. If people saw a ממזרת taken through יבום, they might think a ממזרת is allowed in general.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, the מצוה of יבום would override the לאו of ממזרת. But a regular ישראל may not marry a ממזרת when there is no יבום. So the רבנן also forbade it in the יבום case, so that no one would conclude that a ממזרת is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A protective rule made by the רבנן to keep people from making a mistake.
Where there is a מצוה, here meaning the case where יבום applies.
Because of, out of concern for.

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a general principle: the רבנן can block a מצוה case because it may be confused with a non-מצוה case. The rest of this section tests how far that principle goes.

phrases.english: A decree where there is a מצוה
because of where there is no מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּזֵירָה בִּמְקוֹם מִצְוָה אַטּוּ שֶׁלֹּא בִּמְקוֹם מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 11 by giving a different reason for the גזירה that fits the ממזרת and נתינה cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Broadens the reason for the גזירה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The only reason for the ban is confusion with a similar always-forbidden widow, so ממזרת and נתינה have no reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban can also come from the worry that allowing her in a מצוה case will make people think she is allowed when there is no מצוה.

steps.title: Then block יבום with a paternal brother's wife too
steps.stepSummary: If confusion is enough for a גזירה, the wife of a brother from the same father should not have יבום, because people might confuse it with a brother from the same mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, the wife of his brother from his father should not have יבום, as a גזירה because of the wife of his brother from his mother!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the principle from Step 12 further to show a problem. If the רבנן ban things because of possible confusion, they should have banned normal יבום too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יבום only applies to a brother from the same father. The wife of a brother from the same mother only is always forbidden. By the logic of Step 12, the רבנן should have forbidden even regular יבום so people would not mix the two up. Since they did not, the principle seems too broad.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But now', meaning: if your reasoning is true, then look what follows.
The wife of his brother who has the same father. This is where יבום applies.
The wife of his brother who has only the same mother. She is always forbidden.
She will be taken in יבום.

phrases.english: But now, if so,
the wife of his paternal brother should not have levirate marriage,
as a decree because of the wife of his maternal brother!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, אֵשֶׁת אָחִיו מֵאָבִיו לֹא תִּתְיַיבֵּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 12 by showing that its principle would also cancel ordinary יבום.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle of 'גזירה במקום מצוה אטו שלא במקום מצוה'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A reductio: if confusion is enough for a גזירה, even normal יבום should be banned because of the maternal brother's wife, which is clearly not the halacha.

steps.title: יבום is tied to inheritance, which everyone knows
steps.stepSummary: The Torah tied יבום to inheritance, and everyone knows only paternal relatives inherit, so no one will be confused.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah made יבום depend on inheritance; it is well known.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this case is different, because there is no real risk of confusion. The Torah linked יבום to inheritance, and everyone knows that inheritance goes through the father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה is only needed when people are likely to make a mistake. Since it is common knowledge that brothers inherit through the father, everyone understands why only a paternal brother does יבום. The maternal brother's case will not get mixed up.

keyTerms.meaning: Marriage of a childless widow by her late husband's brother.
Inheritance.
'The Merciful One (the Torah) made it depend on'.
'It is surely known' – common knowledge, so no one will err.

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the principle of Step 12 is wrong. It is saying a גזירה is only made where people might actually be confused, and here they would not be.

phrases.english: The Merciful One made levirate marriage depend on inheritance,
it is well known.
phrases.notes: Everyone knows only relatives through the father inherit, so no one will mix this up.

steps.triggerLanguage: יִיבּוּם בְּנַחֲלָה תְּלָא רַחְמָנָא, מִידָּע יְדִיעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 13 by showing that there is no real chance of confusion in that case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any two similar-looking cases call for a גזירה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A גזירה is only needed when the line between the cases is not clear. Here the Torah's condition (inheritance) is common knowledge.

steps.title: Then block יבום for a childless widow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a childless widow is not barred from יבום because of a widow who has children.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who has no children should not have יבום, as a גזירה because of a woman who has children!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second case to test the same principle. A widow with children may never marry her husband's brother, so why not ban יבום for a childless widow too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the two cases look the same: both are a brother's widow. The only difference is whether the dead brother left children. The גמרא asks why that difference would not cause confusion and call for a גזירה.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow without children. This is when יבום applies.
A widow with children. She stays forbidden to the brother.
The ceremony that releases a widow from יבום. It would replace יבום if יבום were banned.

phrases.aramaic: אִשָּׁה שֶׁאֵין לָהּ בָּנִים לֹא תִּתְיַיבֵּם,
phrases.english: A woman who has no children should not have levirate marriage,

phrases.aramaic: גְּזֵירָה מִשּׁוּם אִשָּׁה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ בָּנִים!
phrases.english: as a decree because of a woman who has children!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִשָּׁה שֶׁאֵין לָהּ בָּנִים לֹא תִּתְיַיבֵּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge of the same type as Step 13, using a different pair of cases.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle of 'גזירה במקום מצוה אטו שלא במקום מצוה'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A widow with and without children look alike, so by the same logic יבום should be banned, which it is not.

steps.title: יבום is tied to having no children, which everyone knows
steps.stepSummary: The Torah tied יבום to the absence of children, and everyone knows this, so there will be no confusion.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah made it depend on children; it is well known.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same kind of answer as before. Everyone knows יבום is only for a man who died without children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that יבום only applies when there are no children is a basic, well-known part of the Torah's law. So seeing יבום with a childless widow will never lead people to allow a widow who has children.

keyTerms.meaning: On children, meaning on whether the dead brother left children.

phrases.english: The Merciful One made it depend on children,
it is well known.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 15 using the same 'well known' reasoning as Step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Widows with and without children might be confused.
steps.terutzMaskana: The condition of having no children is common knowledge, so no גזירה is needed.

steps.title: Then block יבום for a brother who lived at the same time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why יבום is not banned for a brother who was alive together with the dead brother, because of a brother born after he died.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wife of his brother who was in his world should not have יבום, as a גזירה because of the wife of his brother who was not in his world!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a third case to test the principle. A brother born after the dead brother died does not do יבום, so why not ban יבום for every brother?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two brothers who were alive at the same time do יבום. A brother born only after the death does not. These cases look alike, so the גמרא asks why there is no גזירה here too.

keyTerms.meaning: Who was 'in his world', meaning alive at the same time as the dead brother.
Who was not alive at the same time, meaning born after the brother died.

phrases.aramaic: אֵשֶׁת אָחִיו שֶׁהָיָה בְּעוֹלָמוֹ לֹא תִּתְיַיבֵּם,
phrases.english: The wife of his brother who was alive in his lifetime should not have levirate marriage,

phrases.aramaic: גְּזֵרָה מִשּׁוּם אֵשֶׁת אָחִיו שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בְּעוֹלָמוֹ!
phrases.english: as a decree because of the wife of his brother who was not alive in his lifetime!
phrases.notes: He means a brother born only after the husband died. That brother does not do יבום.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵשֶׁת אָחִיו שֶׁהָיָה בְּעוֹלָמוֹ לֹא תִּתְיַיבֵּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third challenge of the same type as Steps 13 and 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle of 'גזירה במקום מצוה אטו שלא במקום מצוה'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Brothers alive at the same time and a brother born after the death look alike, so by the same logic יבום should be banned.

steps.title: יבום is tied to the brothers 'dwelling together', which everyone knows
steps.stepSummary: The Torah tied יבום to brothers living at the same time, and this is clear from the פסוק, so there will be no confusion.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah made it depend on dwelling together; it is well known.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers this case the same way as the others. The Torah says יבום applies when brothers 'dwell together', and everyone knows it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The condition that the brothers lived at the same time is written openly in the פסוק. So no one would think a brother born after the death also does יבום. In all three challenges, a גזירה is only made where people would really be confused.

keyTerms.meaning: Dwelling, meaning the brothers living in the world at the same time.
'When brothers dwell together', the פסוק that sets this condition for יבום.

steps.whatToRemember: A גזירה because of confusion is only made when confusion is likely. Where the Torah tied יבום to a clear, well-known condition (inheritance, no children, brothers living together), no גזירה is needed. The ממזרת and נתינה explanation itself is knocked down soon after, in step 21.

phrases.english: The Merciful One made it depend on dwelling together,
it is well known.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 17 and closes the set of three challenges with the same reasoning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Brothers who lived at the same time might be confused with a brother born after the death.
steps.terutzMaskana: The condition of 'dwelling together' is stated in the פסוק and widely known, so no גזירה is needed.

steps.title: Why not ban יבום for all women because of an אילונית?
steps.stepSummary: Following the same pattern as before, the גמרא asks why the רבנן did not forbid יבום for every woman, so that no one would mistakenly do יבום with an אילונית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let no woman do יבום at all, as a decree because of an אילונית!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more case of 'why not make a decree because of a similar case.' This time it asks about an אילונית, who is not allowed to do יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the רבנן worry that people will mix up cases that look alike, then an ordinary יבמה looks like an אילונית. By that logic, every woman should be banned from יבום so that no one does יבום with an אילונית.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who is physically unable to have children; she does not do יבום
They should do יבום (marry the dead husband's brother)
A rabbinic decree made to keep people away from a mistake

phrases.english: All women should not do יבום,
as a decree because of an אילונית!

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַנָּשִׁים לֹא תִּתְיַיבֵּמְנָה, גְּזֵרָה מִשּׁוּם אַיְלוֹנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another challenge in the same pattern as steps 15 and 17
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the רבנן banned יבום for forbidden women so that people would not confuse them with cases where there is no מצוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If confusion between cases that look alike is enough for a decree, then every יבמה should be banned because of an אילונית

steps.title: An אילונית is rare
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that an אילונית is uncommon, and the רבנן do not make decrees for rare cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not common.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question about the אילונית in two words: it does not happen often.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Decrees are made to stop mistakes that are likely to happen. A rare case like an אילונית is not a real danger, so there is no reason to ban יבום for everyone because of her.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not common; it rarely happens

phrases.english: It is not common.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rarity: no decree is made for an uncommon case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every woman should be banned from יבום because of an אילונית
steps.terutzMaskana: An אילונית is rare, so no decree is needed

steps.title: A ממזרת and a נתינה are also rare
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the answer around: a ממזרת or נתינה who falls to יבום is also rare, so the whole decree for them makes no sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ממזרת and a נתינה are also not common!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the last answer against the whole explanation. If rare cases get no decree, then the decree about a ממזרת and a נתינה should not exist either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The decree we have been defending is that a ממזרת or נתינה may not do יבום, so people won't come to marry her without a מצוה. But these cases are also uncommon. By the rule just given, the רבנן would not decree here, so the explanation falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman born from a forbidden union; forbidden to marry a regular Jew
A woman descended from the גבעונים; forbidden to marry a regular Jew

phrases.english: A ממזרת and a נתינה are also not common!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of step 20 to knock down the whole decree explanation
steps.kashyaTarget: The basic explanation that יבום with forbidden women was banned to prevent marriage to them without a מצוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If rare cases get no decree, and a ממזרת or נתינה falling to יבום is also rare, then there is no reason for this decree

steps.title: רבא: the first ביאה is banned because of the second
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a new reason. The first ביאה of יבום is a מצוה, but the second is not. So the רבנן banned even the first one, so that he would not go on to the second.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: there is a decree on the first ביאה because of the second ביאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The old explanation failed, so רבא offers a completely new reason why these women only do חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ביאה with the יבמה fulfills the עשה of יבום, and that עשה pushes aside the לאו. After that, the מצוה is done, so the second ביאה is just a plain sin. Since a man who marries her will keep living with her, the רבנן banned even the first ביאה.

keyTerms.meaning: The first act of marital relations, which completes the מצוה of יבום
Any later act of relations, which is no longer part of the מצוה
Because of; out of concern for

phrases.english: Rather, רבא said:
There is a decree on the first ביאה
because of the second ביאה.
phrases.notes: After the first time the מצוה is done, so the second time is simply forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: גְּזֵרָה בִּיאָה רִאשׁוֹנָה אַטּוּ בִּיאָה שְׁנִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation knocked down in step 21
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The decree was meant to stop people from confusing יבום with marriage that involves no מצוה
steps.terutzMaskana: The decree was meant to stop the second, non-מצוה ביאה

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that if they did יבום, the first ביאה works, but he may not keep her for a second ביאה. This matches רבא's reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: if they had relations, they acquired her with the first ביאה, but it is forbidden to keep them for a second ביאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that fits רבא's new reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sees a real difference between the first ביאה, which works and acquires her, and the second, which is forbidden. That is the same split רבא used to explain the decree.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא also teaches this, as support
They acquired her as a wife
To keep them (stay married to them)

phrases.english: A ברייתא also teaches this:
If they had relations, they acquired her with the first ביאה,
phrases.notes: "They" means a יבם who did יבום with one of the forbidden women anyway.

phrases.english: but it is forbidden to keep them for a second ביאה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's reason from step 22
steps.raayaObject: רבא's idea that the first ביאה and the second ביאה are different
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: the first ביאה acquires her, but keeping her for a second ביאה is forbidden

steps.title: רבא takes back his reason and quotes ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: רבא (or רב אשי) says his decree explanation was wrong. The real reason comes from ריש לקיש: a עשה pushes aside a לא תעשה only when there is no way to keep both.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא then said, and some say it was רב אשי: what I said is not right. For ריש לקיש said: anywhere you find a עשה and a לא תעשה, if you can keep both of them, that is best. If not, let the עשה come and push aside the לא תעשה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא changes his mind about his own answer. He brings ריש לקיש's general rule to set up a simpler, Torah-level explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No rabbinic decree is needed at all. By ריש לקיש's rule, a עשה only beats a לא תעשה when there is no other choice. If both can be kept, the עשה never overrides the לאו.

keyTerms.meaning: He then said; he went back and changed his view
And some say (it was said by someone else)
It is not correct; it is nothing
A positive מצוה and a prohibition
Let the עשה come and push aside (the לאו)

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying that a עשה never overrides a לאו. He is saying it only does so when there is no way to keep both.

phrases.aramaic: הֲדַר אָמַר רָבָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: רבא then said, and some say it was רב אשי:
What I said is not correct,
phrases.notes: He means his own reason from step 22, the decree on the first ביאה.

phrases.english: for ריש לקיש said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁאַתָּה מוֹצֵא עֲשֵׂה וְלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה,
phrases.english: Anywhere you find a positive command and a prohibition,

phrases.aramaic: אִם אַתָּה יָכוֹל לְקַיֵּים שְׁנֵיהֶם — מוּטָב,
phrases.english: if you are able to keep both of them, that is best,
and if not, let the positive command come
and push aside the prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר אָמַר רָבָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב אָשֵׁי: לָאו מִילְּתָא הִיא דַּאֲמַרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא retracts the reason he gave in step 22 and brings a general rule instead
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבא's own explanation that this is a rabbinic decree on the first ביאה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: No decree is needed, because by ריש לקיש's rule the עשה does not override the לאו here at all
steps.whyThisMatters: ריש לקיש's rule shows up all over ש״ס: a עשה overrides a לא תעשה only when you cannot keep both.

steps.title: Here, חליצה keeps both
steps.stepSummary: Applying ריש לקיש's rule: through חליצה, the brother fulfills the מצוה and does not break the לאו. So יבום with these women stays forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is possible through חליצה, which keeps the עשה and the לא תעשה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies ריש לקיש's rule to our case and finishes the new explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה with a יבמה can be done either by יבום or by חליצה. With a forbidden woman, חליצה fulfills the עשה without breaking the לאו. Since both can be kept, the עשה of יבום does not push aside the לאו, so these women do חליצה and not יבום, straight from the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: The ceremony that releases the יבמה from the brother instead of יבום
It is possible

steps.whatToRemember: This is רבא's retracted view: since חליצה keeps both the עשה and the לאו, the עשה of יבום would not override the לאו. Step 27 rejects this view, and the rabbinic decree reason stands.

phrases.english: Here too, it is possible through חליצה,
which keeps both the positive command and the prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי אֶפְשָׁר בַּחֲלִיצָה, דִּמְקַיֵּים עֲשֵׂה וְלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies ריש לקיש's rule from step 24 to the case of the forbidden יבמה
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא's proposal: since חליצה fulfills the מצוה without breaking the לאו, the עשה of יבום does not override the לאו. This proposal is refuted in step 27.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the ביאה still acquires her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא's explanation from ריש לקיש with a ברייתא saying that if they had ביאה, they acquired the woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: 'And if they had relations, they acquired her.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to attack רבא's newest explanation from step 24-25.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to ריש לקיש's rule, the עשה of יבום should not push aside the לאו at all, because חליצה is possible. But the ברייתא says that if they did יבום anyway, they acquired her as a wife. That means the עשה did push aside the לאו, so the ban cannot come from ריש לקיש's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged (from a ברייתא or משנה)
They had relations (ביאה)
They acquired her as a wife

phrases.english: They challenged: And if they had relations, they acquired her.
phrases.notes: "They" means the brothers doing יבום with these women who are forbidden to them by a לאו.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the conclusion of step 25, which was based on ריש לקיש's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's explanation that יבום here stays forbidden because ריש לקיש's rule says the עשה cannot push aside the לאו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the עשה did not push aside the לאו, the ביאה would not acquire her. The ברייתא says it does acquire her, so the עשה must push the לאו aside.

steps.title: Full refutation of רבא's last explanation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares the challenge a full refutation, so the explanation from ריש לקיש falls away.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rules that the ברייתא completely knocks down רבא's last explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since ריש לקיש's rule cannot explain the ban, we go back to the earlier explanation from step 22: the ban is a rabbinic decree. The first ביאה is a מצוה and works, but the רבנן forbade it so that he would not go on to a second ביאה.

keyTerms.meaning: A full refutation; the view is rejected

steps.whatToRemember: The ban on יבום with women forbidden by a לאו is a rabbinic decree, not a Torah-level rule. That is why the ביאה still acquires her if it was done.

phrases.english: A refutation.
phrases.notes: This means רבא's explanation from ריש לקיש is rejected, and the earlier "rabbinic decree" reason stands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge of step 26 by accepting it as decisive.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ריש לקיש's rule does not explain this case. The ban is a rabbinic decree, and a ביאה that was done still acquires her.

steps.title: A כהן גדול who does יבום with a widow: does it free the צרה?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר argue whether a כהן גדול's ביאה with his widowed יבמה frees her צרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: the ביאה of a כהן גדול with a widow. רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר: one said it does not free her צרה, and one said it does free her צרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new related topic: an argument between two אמוראים about a כהן גדול who did יבום with his brother's widow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן גדול may not marry a widow, so this יבום was forbidden. One view says a forbidden ביאה like this does not free the other wife (the צרה) from יבום. The other view says that even though it was forbidden, it still counts as יבום, so the צרה is free.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (a dispute between אמוראים)
The High Priest
A widow, forbidden to a כהן גדול
Frees, exempts
Her co-wife (the other wife of the dead brother)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not say which of the two, רבי יוחנן or רבי אלעזר, holds which view. It only says "one said" and "one said."

phrases.english: It was stated: the relations of a כהן גדול with a widow.
phrases.notes: The widow here is his יבמה, his dead brother's wife. A כהן גדול may not marry a widow (ויקרא 21:14).

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Elazar disagree:
One said: it does not free her co-wife,
and one said: it frees her co-wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion on the same theme: יבום with a woman forbidden to the brother by a לאו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dispute: one view says a כהן גדול's ביאה with his widowed יבמה does not free her צרה. The other view says it does free her צרה.
